interpretation: On the held-out sample the matcher accepted 0 pair(s) that the reviewer labelled different and withheld 15 of 72 true matches. Precision is 100.0% (57/57; Wilson 95% 93.7-100.0%); recall is 79.2% (57/72; Wilson 95% 68.4-86.9%).
No accepted pair was wrong in this sample while some true matches were not accepted, so the policy favours precision over recall on this sample.

Decisive coverage is 48.5% (94/194; Wilson 95% 41.5-55.4%): 30 of 194 binary pairs ended as UNRESOLVED and 70 as CONFLICT (not decided), and decisive accuracy (accuracy among the decided pairs) is 100.0% (94/94; Wilson 95% 96.1-100.0%).
ExactIdentifier path: TP 55, FP 0, FN 0 of 55 binary pairs. Those pairs were sampled because they share an observed identifier, so this is not a test of identifier-free matching.
False negatives by matching path: Scored 15; Scored-path recall is 11.8% (2/17; Wilson 95% 3.3-34.3%).
Read these figures with the intervals above and the sample limits; no claim about the whole corpus follows from this evaluation.

threats_to_validity: Convenience sample: the 300 queued pairs (200 held-out and 40 development initial reviews, 60 reserves never reviewed) were drawn from candidate pairs by oversampled evidence strata (shared observed id, observed id disagreement, missing authoritative id) with no population weights. The rates are rates in this sample, not rates in the full candidate population (the 5E report states 11,412 decisions) or the corpus.

The sampling strata are defined by the evidence the matcher itself uses (a shared observed identifier selects the ExactIdentifier path), so per-path precision and recall are partly determined by how the stratum was built.

Labels are AI-assisted: a language model drafted the labels and one human reviewer ticked checkboxes; 22 Researcher labels (the exclusion file; per the 5E report 18 held-out and 4 development) used external source checks whose evidence was not retained (self-attested). The 'without 22 assisted' slice removes those 22, but the other labels remain AI-drafted, so neither slice is independent blind gold, and there is a single reviewer, so inter-annotator agreement is unmeasured.

No calibration or threshold tuning was done; the policy is er-offline-uncalibrated-v2 and was not changed for this evaluation. Development sensitivity analysis (eight hypothetical cutoffs) is outside this package and is not calibration.

Blocking recall (whether true matches ever reach the candidate pair list) and global identity recall are unmeasured, so a pair the blocker never proposed is invisible here. Recall here is recall among the proposed, sampled pairs.

The course asks for 200 manually reviewed examples. This sample has 200 held-out plus 40 development reviewed pairs; 6 held-out and 2 development pairs are uncertain and not scored, which leaves 194 held-out binary labels. The labels are human-reviewed but AI-drafted (see above).
Zero observed false positives (precision 100%) is a statement about this sample: the Wilson upper bound of the false merge rate is reported above and is not zero.
Common-name and unobserved cross-partition leakage risks remain (the split groups known source, identifier and title anchors only).
The LLM-adjudicated path has no observations (disabled by configuration), and no real provider was called; nothing here speaks to LLM-assisted identity decisions.
